fluff.overview:
The Chippewa is a ninety-ton heavy aerospace fighter commissioned in 2584 by Bowie Industries for the Star League Defense Force. Designed to provide overwhelming firepower during the Reunification War campaigns against the Periphery states, the Chippewa was built to close with enemy formations and deliver devastating strikes at short and medium range. Its large, swept-wing airframe provides surprising atmospheric agility for a craft of its size, with retractable wingtips that allow it to be stored compactly aboard carrier vessels.

The Chippewa became synonymous with the Lyran Commonwealth after the fall of the Star League, serving as House Steiner's primary heavy fighter for centuries. Licensed production by Vandenberg Mechanized Industries on New Vandenberg also ensured a steady supply to the Taurian Concordat. Though never the fastest or most agile heavy fighter in service, the Chippewa earned a fearsome reputation through the sheer volume of fire it could bring to bear on any target foolish enough to remain in its sights.
fluff.capabilities:
The CHP-W5 Chippewa prioritizes firepower above all other considerations. Its primary armament consists of four McCorkel large lasers mounted in the wings, capable of shredding medium fighters in a single pass. Two Exostar LRM-15 racks provide long-range striking power during approach runs, while an Exostar SRM-6 and two Martell medium lasers in the nose deliver additional punishment at close range. Two McCorkel small lasers mounted in the tail discourage pursuit by lighter dogfighters.

The Bowie 50 airframe is powered by a PlasmaStar 270 fusion engine, providing adequate but unspectacular thrust for a ninety-ton fighter. Twenty-five single heat sinks manage the substantial thermal load generated by the laser-heavy weapons suite, though sustained fire from all weapons simultaneously will still push heat levels into uncomfortable territory. Early Star League production models featured specialized laser insulators developed by Bowie that gave the large lasers additional cooling capacity, though the knowledge to produce this insulation was lost during the Succession Wars.

Protection is the Chippewa's most notable weakness. The Wyatt Coresteel Standard armor provides only modest coverage for a heavy fighter, leaving the craft vulnerable to concentrated fire. Pilots quickly learn to rely on the Chippewa's firepower advantage to eliminate threats before they can exploit this shortcoming. Rander 200 communications and Rander TAS targeting systems provide reliable if unremarkable sensor coverage.
fluff.deployment: The CHP-W10 is a Federated Suns field modification of the standard CHP-W5 that sacrifices offensive capability for dramatically improved survivability. Two of the four large lasers are removed, freeing tonnage for an additional nine and a half tons of armor. This more than doubles the Chippewa's protection, transforming it from one of the most thinly armored heavy fighters into a reasonably well-protected platform. House Davion units favor this configuration for missions requiring sustained engagement rather than hit-and-run strikes, finding that the remaining two large lasers combined with the full missile complement still provide adequate firepower against most targets.
fluff.history:
The Chippewa entered service with the SLDF in 2584, arriving just as the Reunification War was reaching its most intense phase. Bowie Industries operated primary production facilities on Dell and Wasat, both under contract to the Star League military. The fighter proved its worth during the Periphery campaigns, where its heavy weapons loadout made it effective at suppressing ground defenses and engaging the lighter fighters fielded by the Periphery nations. A Royal variant, the CHP-W5b, was introduced in 2731 with upgraded technology including an extralight engine, extended-range lasers, and double heat sinks, though this model was restricted to SLDF Royal units and its production was limited to Dell and Wasat.

The fall of the Star League dramatically reshaped the Chippewa's production theater. The Wasat facility, operated under Terran Hegemony oversight, was presumed destroyed during the Amaris Coup. The Lyran Commonwealth seized the Bowie Industries plant on Dell prior to the First Succession War, maintaining production of the CHP-W5 and earlier Star League models until House Kurita successfully destroyed the facility in a devastating raid around 2805. This left the Alarion plant, which Bowie had relocated production to at the start of the Succession Wars, as the sole Inner Sphere source. The Commonwealth managed to keep the Alarion line running, slowly rebuilding Chippewa stocks while other operators watched their fleets dwindle through attrition.

The Taurian Concordat secured a manufacturing license from Bowie, with Vandenberg Mechanized Industries on New Vandenberg beginning production of the CHP-W5. This arrangement gave the Concordat its own domestic source of heavy fighters, ensuring continued Chippewa availability in the Periphery. Bowie Industries also operated a significant production facility on Wyatt, which became a key source of upgraded Chippewa models alongside Alarion.

As technology recovery accelerated in the late thirty-first century, Bowie developed the CHP-W7 upgrade incorporating double heat sinks, an extralight engine, ferro-aluminum armor, and pulse laser variants. Production of the W7 began at both Alarion and Wyatt during the Clan Invasion era. The Federated Suns had meanwhile developed their own field modification, the CHP-W10, which traded two large lasers for substantially improved armor protection, addressing the design's most persistent criticism.

The Jihad struck the Chippewa's production network hard. The Word of Blake destroyed the Bowie Industries facility on Wyatt with nuclear weapons in 3068, eliminating a major source of upgraded models. Prior to the Blakist assault on Alarion, Bowie had begun transitioning the W7 line to the CHP-W8 configuration featuring heavy ferro-aluminum armor and MML launchers. Vandenberg Mechanized Industries on New Vandenberg responded to the shifting threat environment by developing the CHP-W7T, incorporating snub-nose PPCs and plasma rifles into the proven W7 platform. The Lyran Alliance had also begun fielding the Eisensturm OmniFighter as a planned successor, though the Chippewa remained in widespread frontline service well into the Dark Age.
